idiom_name: strictNullChecks with optional chaining and Array.prototype.flatMap
implementation_notes: With strictNullChecks on, null and undefined are distinct types and a maybe-absent value cannot be used without narrowing, so absence lives in the type system; optional chaining ?. and nullish coalescing ?? (TypeScript 3.7) make the access concise, and optional properties automatically include undefined in their type. The plural traversal is Array.prototype.flatMap (from lib es2019) together with filter/map, and discriminated unions can model a present/absent focus explicitly; these replace the classic optic structure. The type-level part depends on the compiler option, so without strictNullChecks the runtime behaviour stays but the guarantee is gone.
pitfalls: strictNullChecks is opt-in: without it null and undefined are assignable to every type and the pattern degenerates to unchecked runtime access.
Non-null assertions (!) and as casts silence the checker rather than narrowing, reintroducing runtime undefined at the value's consumers.
Data parsed from JSON is typically any/unknown: optionality must be validated at the boundary or the type system never sees it.
